name: Toronto
tagline: The sandwich Bourdain went back for at the world's best market, and the four-star review that cemented chef Patrick Kriss's reputation.

Sushi Masaki Saito.description: Eleven-seat omakase from chef Masaki Saito, once holding two Michelin stars. Today it holds one.

Carousel Bakery.description: Canada's most famous peameal bacon sandwich, at the St. Lawrence Market — named the world's best market by National Geographic. Bourdain and Bobby Flay both went back for seconds.

Gryfe's Bagel Bakery.description: A Jewish bakery on Bathurst Street since the 1930s, hand-rolling and baking its bagels to the same family recipe for more than three generations.

Alo.description: Contemporary French cuisine from chef Patrick Kriss, atop a heritage downtown building. Michelin star, and a four-star review from critic Chris Nuttall-Smith in The Globe and Mail.

Seven Lives Tacos y Mariscos.description: Baja California-style tacos in the heart of Kensington Market, one of the neighborhood's most beloved spots.

Shoushin.description: Chef Jackie Lin's Edomae omakase at a hinoki counter on Yonge Street, with a menu that shifts with the day's fish. Earned its Michelin star in Toronto's inaugural guide in 2022.

Restaurant 20 Victoria.description: A contemporary tasting menu with Mexican flourishes from chef Rafa Covarrubias, served in an intimate Financial District dining room. Holds one Michelin star.

DaNico.description: Chef Daniele Corona's Italian cooking with global accents, inside a restored early-1900s bank building in Little Italy — the wine cellar sits in the old vault. Earned its Michelin star in 2024.

Aburi Hana.description: Seasonal Japanese kaiseki in Yorkville, holding a Michelin star since Toronto's first guide in 2022.

Alma.description: Chef Anna Chen's contemporary Chinese cooking in Bloordale Village. Holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2022.

Sunnys Chinese.description: A high-energy spot for authentic Chinese flavours in Kensington Market, from the team behind Mimi. Holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Giulietta.description: Chefs Rob Rossi and David Minicucci's neighbourhood trattoria on College Street, known for wood-fired pizza and house-made pasta. Holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Bar Raval.description: Chef Grant van Gameren's Spanish tapas bar, with a hand-carved curved wood facade inspired by Barcelona. Holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand and has repeatedly ranked among Canada's best bars.

Enoteca Sociale.description: A Rome-inspired trattoria in Little Portugal known for hand-made pasta. Holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2022.

Porchetta & Co.description: Slow-roasted porchetta sandwiches, one of the spots Anthony Bourdain visited and recommended during his Toronto stop on The Layover.

Sneaky Dee's.description: A Tex-Mex bar and concert venue on College Street since 1987, an Anthony Bourdain stop on The Layover and a pillar of Toronto's indie music scene.

The Burger's Priest.description: A burger chain born in Toronto in 2010, recommended by Anthony Bourdain during his Toronto episode of The Layover.

Bar Isabel.description: Chef Grant van Gameren's Spanish tapas and seafood spot on College Street, one of the most critically acclaimed restaurants in Toronto since it opened in 2013.

United Bakers Dairy Restaurant.description: A Jewish dairy restaurant founded in 1912 by a young couple from Kielce, the oldest of its kind in Canada, now on Lawrence Avenue West.

Rol San.description: Cantonese dim sum served all day since 1994 in the heart of Chinatown, one of the city's first spots to offer it outside traditional morning hours.

Swatow Restaurant.description: A no-frills Cantonese diner on Spadina Avenue, serving fast, authentic Chinese food into the late night for more than 40 years.

Fran's Restaurant.description: A Canadian diner open since 1940, one of Toronto's oldest restaurants, known for round-the-clock breakfast.

The Senator.description: Opened in 1929 as the Busy Bee Diner and renamed The Senator in 1948, it's Toronto's oldest restaurant still operating at its original address.

Café Diplomatico.description: An Italian cafe-pizzeria opened in 1968 by the Mastrangelo brothers at the heart of College Street, one of the first Italian-owned spots in Little Italy.

Messini Authentic Gyros.description: Greek gyros on Danforth Avenue since 2003, credited as the first spot in the neighbourhood to introduce Greek-style fries.

Le Sélect Bistro.description: A classic French bistro opened in 1977, with one of Toronto's most extensive wine lists; it marks half a century in the city in 2027.

Terroni.description: An Italian restaurant opened in 1992 on Queen Street West, a pioneer in bringing Neapolitan pizza and imported Italian goods to Toronto.

Wanda's Pie in the Sky.description: A Kensington Market bakery known for its handmade pies and desserts, a neighbourhood classic since the 1990s.

Patois.description: Chef Craig Wong's Chinese-Jamaican cooking on Dundas Street West, blending his family heritage with techniques learned at Heston Blumenthal's The Fat Duck.

Ali's West Indian Roti Shop.description: A Caribbean roti shop in Parkdale serving Trinidadian-style stuffed roti for more than four decades, a staple of Toronto's Indo-Caribbean community.

Pai Northern Thai Kitchen.description: Chefs Nuit and Jeff Regular's Northern Thai cooking in the Entertainment District, a fixture on Toronto food critics' must-try lists.

Banh Mi Boys.description: Vietnamese sandwiches with Korean touches on Queen Street West, one of the spots that popularized the banh mi-taco fusion in Toronto.

Mother's Dumplings.description: Hand-made dumplings following a family recipe from Northeast China, in the heart of Chinatown since chef Zhen Feng opened it in 2005.

Byblos.description: Contemporary Eastern Mediterranean cooking in the Entertainment District, with mezze and grilled dishes praised by Toronto critics.

Nadège Patisserie.description: A French pastry shop founded in 2009 by chef Nadège Nourian, a fourth-generation Lyon-born pastry chef, in the heart of Queen West.

Kinka Izakaya.description: A boisterous Japanese izakaya on Church Street, where servers shout out orders in traditional style — one of Toronto's most popular izakaya chains.

Canoe.description: Contemporary Canadian cuisine on the 54th floor of the TD Bank Tower, with panoramic views over Lake Ontario — a Toronto fine-dining institution since 1995.

Scaramouche.description: A special-occasion restaurant in South Hill since 1980, with chef Keith Froggett leading its classic French-Canadian kitchen since 1983.

Richmond Station.description: Seasonal restaurant from chef Carl Heinrich, winner of Top Chef Canada season two, at the corner of Yonge and Richmond.

Chubby's Jamaican Kitchen.description: Home-style Jamaican cooking in an 1890s downtown row house, with its oxtail poutine singled out by the Michelin Guide.
